SYC.note: Strategy safeguards described as intended; no AI rule or authority stated.
Government AI uses are only proposed applications; none piloted or in service.
Healthcare and other AI uses are only proposed; none piloted or in service.

facts.fact: Cabinet approved the Seychelles Digital and AI Strategy 2026-2031 on Wednesday 28 October 2026, projected to cost $50 million over five years, says the Seychelles News Agency.

Cabinet also approved an Inter-Ministerial Digital and AI Coordination Committee chaired by the Vice-President to support implementation, and a Digital Transformation Division monitors delivery, says Principal Secretary Choppy.
facts.system: Inter-Ministerial Digital and AI Coordination Committee

facts.fact: The government cloud project approved under the strategy will provide AI computing infrastructure located in Seychelles for government use, with implementation expected mid-2027 to mid-2028 and World Bank support, says Principal Secretary Choppy.
The approved strategy includes digital and AI training for civil servants, with initial initiatives expected during 2027 and early 2028, says Principal Secretary Choppy.

SYC.note: A sovereign government cloud is planned; no hosting policy or rule stated, so it is not the study's class.
Government data centres planned, not for hire and not in service.
Refers to national data protection and privacy laws only in passing; no law named or dated.

facts.fact: The approved strategy includes digital literacy programmes, with initial initiatives expected during 2027 and early 2028, says Principal Secretary Choppy.

The approved strategy's first major project is a sovereign government cloud on two geographically separated data centres, with AI computing kept in Seychelles to address sovereignty and sensitive government data, says Principal Secretary Choppy.

SYC.note: Government data centres planned for 2027-2028; none in service stated.
